title: Two moments, one line each

steps.say: range(date) keeps the first and the last quarter. Two bars per region, 26 in all: the change is in there, but the reader has to compare pairs across a crowded axis.
Put the two quarters on the axis and join each region's two points. The slope is the change: twelve lines go down, one goes up.
Colour by a rule: rose is TRUE where the last rate is above the first. arrange(rose) puts the risers last, so they are drawn on top and no grey line crosses them.
Label only the line you talk about, at both ends; the other twelve stay as context. The hjust column puts each label on the outer side of its point.
The title says what the slope shows, and R writes both the region and the size of the change. Test the rule before you trust it: with real data, two regions might rise, or none.

final:
---
title: "What changed"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
ends <- read_csv("unemployment.csv") |>
  filter(region != "Kingdom",
         date %in% range(date)) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(rose = last(rate) > first(rate)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(rose)
riser <- ends |>
  filter(rose) |>
  mutate(hjust = if_else(date == min(date),
                         1.5, -0.5))
change <- last(riser$rate) - first(riser$rate)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot(ends, aes(quarter, rate, group = region,
                 colour = rose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#00803A",
                                 `FALSE` = "grey75"),
                      guide = "none") +
  geom_text(
    data = riser,
    aes(label = scales::number(rate, accuracy = 0.1),
        hjust = hjust),
    size = 4.5) +
  labs(title = str_glue(
         "Only {riser$region[1]} is higher than in ",
         "{min(ends$quarter)}, by {change} points"),
       subtitle = "Unemployment rate, %, all regions",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
